paper text.text:
\begin{lemma}\label{r2:degree-four}
No three-connected obstruction has twin pairs with neighborhoods $\{a,b,c\},\{a,b,d\}$ and $\deg(b)=4$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Suppose $\deg(b)=4$. Every component outside $\Psi_2$
then has neighborhood $\{a,c,d\}$ by three-connectivity.
Let $B_1$ consist of their bridges and $cd$, if present,
so $G=\Psi_2\cup B_1$. By minimality, $G-z$ has a torus
embedding. All bridges in $B_1$ lie in the same face $F$
of $H=\Psi_2-z$, since each meets $d$ and $\deg_H(d)=1$. Record only $a,c,d$ on the boundary walks of $F$.
If consecutive appearances are equal, move their incident
edges to one appearance along the intervening boundary arc,
preserving their order. Since $B_1$ meets both $c,d$,
the rotation table~\supp{R5} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement} leave only the disk sequences
$acd,acad,acacd$ and the annular pairs $ad\mid ac,ad\mid c$. We show that $B_1$ can be drawn in an annulus with $a_1,d$
on one boundary and $a_2,c$ on the other, allowing the edges
at $a$ to use $a_1$ or $a_2$. The annular cases already give
this, with $a_2$ unused for $ad\mid c$. In a disk case,
separate the appearances and use the boundary order
$a_1,c_1,a_2,c_2,d$, leaving positions unused where needed.
Draw $c_1c_2,c_1a_2,a_1d$ outside the disk without crossings,
then contract $c_1c_2$ to recover $c$. The resulting graph
is planar, with $a_1,a_2$ distinct and $a_1d,a_2c$ added.
Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} gives the required drawing (Figure~\ref{fig:psi2-annulus-construction}(d)--(f)). A planar embedding of $\Psi_2$ has faces $apcqa$ and $ardza$.
Remove an open disk from each and join the new boundary
circles by a cylinder. This gives a torus embedding with
an annular face $ac\mid ad$. Insert the drawing of $B_1$,
with the edges at $a_2$ reaching $a$ between $ap,aq$ and
those at $a_1$ reaching $a$ between $ar,az$.
This embeds $G$ on the torus (Figure~\ref{fig:psi2-annulus-construction}(a)--(c)), a contradiction.
\end{proof}

what: Every rotation system of Psi_2 - z. Attachments a, b, c, d; twins omitted. The claim retains only a, c, d, as the text does.
how to read: For each graph: 'cyclic orders' lists, for every vertex, all cyclic orders of its neighbours, each starting with its alphabetically first neighbour (the other neighbours follow in every possible order, in lexicographic order). Rotation system number i (counting from 0) takes at each vertex the cyclic order whose position is the corresponding digit of i, written in the mixed radix given by the numbers of cyclic orders in the order of 'vertices', the last vertex varying fastest (the order of Python's itertools.product). Facial walks are traced by the rule used throughout the supplement: after the dart u->v comes v->w, where w follows u in the cyclic order at v. The genus is (2 - V + E - F)/2. The attachment sequence of a facial walk lists the attachments it passes through, in walk order, one entry per passage; it is written from its lexicographically least cyclic shift, keeping the direction of the walk, and the faces of a row are sorted. Since many rotation systems give the same row, the distinct rows are listed once under 'distinct rows' and 'rows' gives, for every rotation system in order, the position of its row in that list. 'Up to cyclic shift and reversal' in the claims means the least sequence among all cyclic shifts of the sequence and of its reverse.

graphs.row format: [genus, attachment sequences of the facial walks]

claims.statement: Retaining only a, c, d in each boundary walk and combining consecutive equal appearances: up to cyclic shift and reversal the boundary attachment sequences are a, ac, ad, c when the neighbourhood has genus zero, and the sequence containing d is ad, acd, acad or acacd when it has genus one.
